profile: Digital Minds Career Development Fellow, Future Impact Group (FIG)
PhD Candidate at UKRI CDT for Accountable, Responsible, and Transparent AI (ART-AI), University of Bath, UK
about: I'm a researcher working at the intersection of technical AI safety and governance, with a special focus on the legal alignment of AI agents and the assessment of frontier AI capabilities. As we accelerate toward a potential intelligence explosion with AI, we need to ensure that these technologies are safe and lawful by aligning them with our human values.

Currently, I'm working on benchmarking how AI agents apply the rule of law to humans and digital minds as part of my Digital Minds Career Development Fellowship. Previously, I've worked with Noam Kolt to evaluate the legal compliance of AI agents with respect to website scraping policies as part of my Pivotal Fellowship. Consequently, I've also collaborated with Ben Brady and Cullen O'Keefe from the Institute for Law & AI on developing a benchmark for law-following capabilities of AI agents.
My work is often published at high-impact venues, including NeurIPS, ACL, EMNLP, ICML, ICLR, and Nature.
Before moving to the UK, I worked as a Senior NLP Researcher in the Human Language Technology Lab at National University in the Philippines.
news: Starting December, I will be a Visiting Fellow at the Institute for Law & AI, working on improving law-following capabilities of AI agent swarms with Cullen O'Keefe and the Legal Frontiers Team.
I have been awarded the Digital Minds Career Development Fellowship by Future Impact Group and will work on benchmarking how AI agents apply the rule of law to humans and digital minds.
My ScrapeBench project from my Pivotal Fellowship has been accepted to NeurIPS 2026. My other co-authored papers, GlobalPIQA and Jarvis-Bench, have also been accepted. Preprints soon!
Two papers, ComplexityMT and a position paper on rethinking compliance in LLMs, have been accepted to EMNLP 2026!
I reached 2,000 citations in Google Scholar.
Invited panel talk at the Workshop on Law-Following AI hosted by the Institute for Law & AI, Centre for the Future of Intelligence in Jesus College, Cambridge.
Dynamic Epistemic Fallback has been accepted to the ICML AI for Law (AI4Law) Workshop.
Scaling Policy Reasoning Traces has been accepted to the ICML Technical AI Governance Research (TAIGR) Workshop.
